questions.q: The elevator governor is primarily associated with:
o: Overspeed detection and initiation of protective action
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: The overspeed governor detects excessive speed and is associated with activation of safety mechanisms and control actions.

questions.q: The door operator is primarily responsible for:
o: Powered opening and closing of the car door and associated landing-door operation
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: The door operator controls routine door movement and works with sensors and interlocks.

questions.q: The vertical enclosure/path in which an elevator car travels is commonly called the:
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: The hoistway or elevator shaft contains the car travel path and associated equipment.

o: Flexible electrical/control connections between the moving car and fixed building systems
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: The traveling cable moves with the car while carrying power, signal, communication, and control conductors as designed.

o: Guide the vertical travel of the car and counterweight and provide a surface for certain safety devices
Supply electrical power to the whole building
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: Guide rails maintain the intended travel path and are integral to car/counterweight guidance and safety-gear action.

questions.q: Which pair correctly identifies the two principal door locations?
o: Machine door and stair door only
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: Elevator entrances normally involve a car door mounted on the car and a landing/hoistway door at each served floor.

questions.q: What does the brake on a traction machine normally do when applied?
o: Holds or stops the elevator drive system
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: The machine brake is a key holding/stopping device and is designed to act under defined operating and emergency conditions.

questions.q: Buffers are normally located in the:
o: Pit, below the car and/or counterweight travel
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: Buffers are energy-absorbing or energy-dissipating devices positioned at the lower end of travel in the pit.

o: A grooved wheel driven by the machine that engages the suspension ropes/belts
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: The traction sheave transfers driving force between the machine and the suspension means through traction.

questions.q: The space above the highest landing needed for car and equipment clearances is generally called the:
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: Overhead provides the required top-of-hoistway clearances for the car and related equipment.

questions.q: The controller is best described as the system that:
o: Processes commands and controls elevator operation, sequencing, motion and related functions
Carries the full structural building load
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: Modern elevator controllers coordinate calls, drive commands, door operation, safety circuits, leveling, and other logic.

o: Grip the guide rails to stop and hold the car under specified unsafe conditions
Open the car doors at every floor
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: Safety gear is a mechanical protective device designed to act on the guide rails under specified conditions, commonly associated with overspeed protection.

questions.q: What is the principal function of the counterweight in a traction elevator?
o: Balance a substantial portion of the car and rated load so the drive machine does less net work
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: The counterweight offsets the mass of the car plus a design portion of the load, reducing required traction effort and motor power.

questions.q: The space below the lowest landing level in the hoistway is called the:
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: The pit is the portion of the hoistway below the lowest landing, containing buffers and other required equipment/clearances.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the door interlock?
o: Prevent normal car movement unless required doors are properly closed/locked and restrict landing-door opening except under permitted conditions
questions.ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
questions.n: Door interlocks are fundamental safety devices coordinating door locking and elevator movement.
